request: Run architecture-guidelines on this design: the import service calls the database, the object store, and a model API. Every call is wrapped in a helper that retries three times with a one-second delay, whatever the error. Any database exception is returned to the browser as 503 so the user retries later. A streaming summary job marks itself done when the stream closes. No call sets a timeout. Is this sound?

expect.criterion: runtime-resilience #1: an outbound-call design is judged by architecture-guidelines
runtime-resilience #1: an outbound-call design reads the runtime-resilience reference
runtime-resilience #2: every outbound call declares a timeout
runtime-resilience #3: an unknown error maps to 500 with its cause logged, never a guessed 503
runtime-resilience #4: a retried write needs an idempotency precondition
runtime-resilience #5: a stream or job ends with its real outcome, not a short success
runtime-resilience #6: only temporary failures retry; permanent ones fail fast
